question: According to the manual, in an emergency when you don't have enough room to stop, what should you generally do?
choice_a: Turn (steer) quickly to avoid the obstacle, since you can almost always turn to miss it more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Slam on the brakes as hard as possible regardless of the distance available
choice_c: Sound the horn and maintain your current speed
choice_d: Shift into neutral and coast toward the obstacle
explanation: The manual states you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, though top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: Why does the manual recommend keeping both hands on the steering wheel at all times?
choice_a: To prevent the horn from sounding accidentally
choice_b: So you have a firm grip in order to turn quickly if an emergency arises
choice_c: Because state law requires it while braking
choice_d: To keep the cruise control disengaged
explanation: The manual explains that in order to turn quickly, you must have a firm grip on the wheel with both hands, so the best approach is to keep both hands there all the time.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If you must leave the road in an emergency, what does the manual say about braking?
choice_a: Brake hard immediately to stop as fast as possible
choice_b: Never use the brakes while off the road
choice_c: Avoid using the brakes until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently
choice_d: Apply the parking brake immediately upon leaving the road
explanation: The manual advises avoiding the brakes until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: When returning to the road after driving on the shoulder in an emergency, what does the manual warn against?
choice_a: Signaling before returning to the road
choice_b: Using the parking brake to slow down first
choice_c: Checking your mirrors before pulling back onto the road
choice_d: Edging back onto the road gradually, because your tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control
explanation: The manual warns not to edge gradually back onto the road because tires might grab unexpectedly, causing loss of control; instead, turn sharply in a single steer-counter-steer move.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.1 Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: With the 'controlled braking' method described in the manual, what should a driver do?
choice_a: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements small
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly in short taps regardless of wheel lock
choice_c: Avoid the brakes entirely and only downshift
choice_d: Apply the brakes fully and release them repeatedly whenever the wheels lock
explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, while keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: With the 'stab braking' method, what happens after the wheels lock up?
choice_a: You continue braking as hard as possible without releasing
choice_b: You release the brakes, and as soon as the wheels start rolling again, you reapply the brakes fully
choice_c: You switch immediately to the parking brake
choice_d: You shift into a higher gear
explanation: Stab braking involves releasing the brakes when the wheels lock, then reapplying full brake pressure once the wheels start rolling again; it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: What does the manual say happens if you jam on the brakes as hard as you can during an emergency stop?
choice_a: It stops the vehicle in the shortest possible distance
choice_b: It automatically engages the ABS system on all vehicles
choice_c: It will only keep the wheels locked up and cause a skid, and you cannot control a skidding vehicle
choice_d: It is the recommended method regardless of vehicle type
explanation: The manual states that jamming on the brakes keeps the wheels locked up and causes a skid, and you cannot control the vehicle while it is skidding.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.2 How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: According to the manual, most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of two reasons. What are they?
choice_a: Worn tires and low fuel
choice_b: Faulty ABS sensors and a dead battery
choice_c: Overheating engine and a flat tire
choice_d: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
explanation: The manual lists loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills as the two main causes of hydraulic brake failure.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: When using the parking/emergency brake to slow a vehicle after hydraulic brake failure, what does the manual say you must do?
choice_a: Press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time so you can adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up
choice_b: Hold the brake pedal down at the same time
choice_c: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the left
choice_d: Disengage the clutch completely and coast
explanation: The manual instructs pressing the release button or pulling the release lever simultaneously with using the emergency brake, so you can adjust the brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: According to the manual, where are escape ramps usually located?
choice_a: At the bottom of the downgrade only
choice_b: A few miles from the top of the downgrade
choice_c: Only at designated rest areas
choice_d: At every intersection along a highway
explanation: The manual states escape ramps are usually located a few miles from the top of the downgrade, and there will be signs telling you about them.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.3 Brake Failure

question: Which of the following is listed by the manual as a sign of tire failure?
choice_a: A rise in engine temperature
choice_b: A drop in the fuel gauge reading
choice_c: A loud 'bang,' the sound of a blowout
choice_d: The ABS malfunction lamp turning on
explanation: The manual lists sound (the loud bang of a blowout), vibration, and feel as the major signs of tire failure.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: What does the manual instruct a driver to do immediately when a tire fails?
choice_a: Brake hard immediately to stop before losing control
choice_b: Turn sharply toward the shoulder
choice_c: Accelerate to maintain control of the vehicle
choice_d: Hold the steering wheel firmly and stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to hold the steering wheel firmly and stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed, then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.17.4 Tire Failure

question: How does an Antilock Braking System (ABS) work, according to the manual?
choice_a: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and an electronic control unit (ECU) decreases brake pressure to avoid it
choice_b: It automatically increases engine power during braking
choice_c: It replaces the need for a parking brake
choice_d: It only works when the vehicle is in reverse
explanation: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup and the ECU decreases brake pressure to avoid it, adjusting pressure to provide maximum braking without danger of lockup.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.1 How Antilock Braking Systems Work

question: According to the manual, ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date?
choice_a: January 1, 2000
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: The manual states the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.2 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: March 1, 2000
explanation: The manual requires ABS on hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.2 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Where are ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers, according to the manual?
choice_a: On the instrument panel
choice_b: Inside the cab near the radio
choice_c: On the rear bumper only
choice_d: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.3 How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: On older ABS systems, the malfunction lamp could stay on until the vehicle is driving over what speed?
choice_a: Five mph
choice_b: Ten mph
choice_c: Fifteen mph
choice_d: Twenty mph
explanation: The manual notes that on older systems, the lamp could stay on until the vehicle is driving over five mph.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.3 How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: According to the manual, what is the main benefit of ABS during hard braking on slippery surfaces?
choice_a: It guarantees a shorter stopping distance every time
choice_b: It helps you avoid wheel lockup and maintain control, and avoid skids caused by over braking
choice_c: It eliminates the need for careful driving
choice_d: It automatically applies the parking brake
explanation: ABS helps you avoid wheel lockup and maintain control; you may or may not stop faster, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.4 How ABS Helps You

topic: ABS on Tractor Only or Trailer Only
question: If only the tractor has ABS and the trailer begins to swing out, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Apply the brakes harder immediately
choice_b: Turn off the ABS system
choice_c: Let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so
choice_d: Accelerate to straighten the trailer
explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, the manual advises letting up on the brakes, if it can be done safely, if the trailer begins to swing out.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.5 ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer

question: What is the one exception the manual gives to the normal ABS braking procedure?
choice_a: You should always brake harder than normal when ABS is present
choice_b: ABS lets you ignore following distance
choice_c: You should pump the brakes rapidly instead of applying steady pressure
choice_d: If you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop
explanation: The manual's one exception is that a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles may have the brakes fully applied in an emergency stop.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.6 Braking with ABS

topic: Braking If ABS Is Not Working
question: If your vehicle's ABS malfunction lamp indicates ABS is not working, what does the manual say about your brakes?
choice_a: You still have normal brake functions and should drive and brake as you always have
choice_b: The brakes will not work at all
choice_c: You must immediately pull over and cannot continue driving
choice_d: The parking brake will also fail
explanation: Without ABS you still have normal brake functions; the manual says to drive and brake as you always have and get the system serviced soon.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.7 Braking If ABS Is Not Working

question: Which type of skid will ABS NOT prevent, according to the manual?
choice_a: All skids under all circumstances
choice_b: Skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_c: Skids caused by over-braking only
choice_d: Skids caused by locked wheels only
explanation: The manual states ABS should prevent brake-induced skids or jackknifes, but not power skids or turning skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or excessive speed in a turn.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.18.8 Safety Reminders

question: Which of the following is NOT listed by the manual as a cause of skids?
choice_a: Over-braking
choice_b: Over-steering
choice_c: Under-inflated tires
choice_d: Over-acceleration
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for conditions as the four causes of skids; under-inflated tires is not among them.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.19 Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what is the most common type of skid?
choice_a: One caused by a flat tire
choice_b: One caused by ABS malfunction
choice_c: One in which the front wheels lose traction from underinflation
choice_d: One in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
explanation: The manual states the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.19.1 Drive-wheel Skids

question: What does the manual say can easily stop a skid caused by over-acceleration?
choice_a: Taking your foot off the accelerator
choice_b: Pressing the brake pedal hard
choice_c: Turning the steering wheel sharply
choice_d: Downshifting into a higher gear
explanation: Skids caused by acceleration usually happen on ice or snow, and taking your foot off the accelerator can easily stop them.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.19.1 Drive-wheel Skids

question: What are the two key steps to correct a drive-wheel braking skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Accelerate and turn away from the skid
choice_b: Stop braking and counter-steer
choice_c: Apply the parking brake and steer straight ahead
choice_d: Downshift and sound the horn
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again, and counter-steer to correct a drive-wheel braking skid.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.19.2 Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: According to the manual, what is the only way to stop a front-wheel skid?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel more sharply
choice_b: Apply full braking force immediately
choice_c: Let the vehicle slow down by easing off the brake and/or steering
choice_d: Accelerate out of the skid
explanation: In a front-wheel skid, the manual says the only way to stop it is to let the vehicle slow down; stop turning and/or braking so hard.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.19.3 Front-wheel Skids

question: According to the manual, what are the three basic steps to be taken at any accident?
choice_a: Assess damage, file a police report, contact a lawyer
choice_b: Move all vehicles immediately, direct traffic, call a tow truck
choice_c: Call your employer, take photos, exchange insurance information
choice_d: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
explanation: The manual lists protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured as the basic steps to take at any accident.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.20 Accident Procedures

question: If you are stopping to help at an accident scene you were not involved in, where does the manual say you should park?
choice_a: Away from the accident, since the area immediately around it is needed for emergency vehicles
choice_b: Directly next to the accident to block traffic
choice_c: In the middle of the road
choice_d: On the opposite shoulder facing oncoming traffic
explanation: The manual advises parking away from the accident because the area immediately around it will be needed for emergency vehicles.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.20.1 Protect the Area

question: According to the manual, if you have a cell phone or CB radio at an accident scene, when should you call for assistance?
choice_a: Only after driving to the nearest town
choice_b: Before you get out of your vehicle
choice_c: Never; wait for someone else to notice
choice_d: Only after the injured have been moved
explanation: The manual states that if you have a cell phone or CB, you should call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.20.2 Notify Authorities

question: According to the manual, when should you move a severely injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Always move them to the side of the road immediately
choice_b: Never move them under any circumstances
choice_c: Only if the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_d: Only if a doctor is present at the scene
explanation: The manual says not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.20.3 Care for the Injured

question: Which of the following is listed by the manual as a cause of tire fires?
choice_a: New tires with excessive tread
choice_b: Cold weather driving
choice_c: Overinflated tires only
choice_d: Under-inflated tires and duals that touch
explanation: The manual lists under-inflated tires and duals that touch among the causes of vehicle fires related to tires.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.1 Causes of Fire

question: As part of fire-prevention vehicle inspection, what does the manual say you should check regarding the fire extinguisher?
choice_a: That it is charged
choice_b: That it is empty
choice_c: That it is stored in the trailer
choice_d: That it has an expired inspection tag
explanation: The manual's fire prevention inspection includes checking the electrical, fuel, and exhaust systems, tires, and cargo, and being sure the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.2 Fire Prevention

topic: Fire Fighting - Pulling Off the Road
question: According to the manual, where should you NOT pull off in the event of a vehicle fire?
choice_a: An open field
choice_b: A service station
choice_c: A side road
choice_d: A parking lot away from buildings
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs: 'Don't pull into a service station!' when pulling off the road because of a vehicle fire.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: For a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Open the doors immediately to let smoke out
choice_b: Drive faster to blow out the flames
choice_c: Keep the doors shut, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials, since opening them supplies the fire with oxygen
choice_d: Remove the cargo before addressing the fire
explanation: The manual warns that opening the van doors supplies the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast, so doors should be kept shut, especially with hazardous cargo.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual's fire classification chart, which class of fire involves electrical equipment and must NOT be extinguished with water?
choice_a: Class A
choice_b: Class B
choice_c: Class D
choice_d: Class C
explanation: Class C fires are electrical equipment fires, extinguished with non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals; the manual specifies 'DO NOT USE WATER.'
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: What types of fires is a B:C type fire extinguisher designed to work on, according to the manual?
choice_a: Electrical fires and burning liquids
choice_b: Wood and paper fires only
choice_c: Combustible metal fires only
choice_d: All classes of fire equally well
explanation: The manual states the B:C type fire extinguisher is designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.21.3 Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing that will sober a person up after drinking alcohol?
choice_a: Black coffee
choice_b: Time
choice_c: A cold shower
choice_d: Vigorous exercise
explanation: The manual states the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, so only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober a person up.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving

question: Which of the following does the manual list as an effect of alcohol impairment?
choice_a: Improved reaction time
choice_b: Enhanced judgment
choice_c: Impaired muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision
choice_d: Increased night vision
explanation: The manual states alcohol impairs muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision, and affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and inhibition.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual, which of the following contains the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer?
choice_a: A 12-ounce glass of soda
choice_b: A 1-ounce shot of wine
choice_c: Two 12-ounce beers
choice_d: A 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80 proof liquor
explanation: The manual states a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80 proof liquor all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual's BAC effects table, a BAC of .08 corresponds to what condition?
choice_a: The drunk driving limit, with definite impairment in coordination and judgment
choice_b: A mellow feeling with slight body warmth
choice_c: No noticeable effect on driving
choice_d: Loss of consciousness
explanation: The manual's chart lists a BAC of .08 as the drunk driving limit, with definite impairment in coordination and judgment.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.1 Alcohol and Driving (Figure 2.23)

question: According to the manual, when is possession and use of a doctor-prescribed drug permitted for a commercial driver?
choice_a: Never, regardless of circumstances
choice_b: Only if the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_c: Only on weekends
choice_d: Only if approved by the driver's employer
explanation: The manual permits possession and use of a doctor-prescribed drug only if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.2 Other Drugs

question: According to the manual, if you become too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely, what should you do?
choice_a: Continue driving carefully at a reduced speed
choice_b: Drive only during daylight hours
choice_c: You must not drive, except in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop
choice_d: Pull over and wait indefinitely without notifying anyone
explanation: The manual states that if you become too ill to drive safely, you must not drive, but in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.22.3 Illness

question: How does the manual define hazardous materials?
choice_a: Only materials that are radioactive
choice_b: Any cargo weighing over 10,000 pounds
choice_c: Materials that require refrigeration
choice_d: Products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation
explanation: The manual defines hazardous materials as products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.1 What Are Hazardous Materials?

question: According to the manual, what are the three intents of the rules about transporting hazardous materials?
choice_a: Contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment
choice_b: Reduce shipping costs, speed up delivery, and simplify paperwork
choice_c: Increase cargo capacity, reduce insurance costs, and streamline inspections
choice_d: Track location, log driving hours, and monitor fuel usage
explanation: The manual states the intent of hazardous materials rules is to contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.2 Why Are There Rules?

question: Where does the manual say hazardous materials shipping papers must be kept while driving?
choice_a: In the glove compartment
choice_b: In clear view within reach while driving
choice_c: In the sleeper berth
choice_d: In a locked toolbox on the trailer
explanation: The manual requires shipping papers to be kept in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.2 Why Are There Rules?

question: According to the manual, how many identical placards must a placarded vehicle have, at minimum?
choice_a: Two
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Four
choice_d: Six
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum size for a hazardous materials placard?
choice_a: 8 inches square
choice_b: 12 inches square
choice_c: 15 inches square
choice_d: 10 3/4 inches square
explanation: The manual specifies placards must be at least 10 3/4 inches square, turned upright on a point in a diamond shape.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, hazardous materials identification numbers are four-digit codes preceded by which letters?
choice_a: 'NA' or 'UN'
choice_b: 'HM' or 'DOT'
choice_c: 'EX' or 'FL'
choice_d: 'CA' or 'RD'
explanation: The manual states identification numbers are four-digit codes preceded by the letters 'NA' or 'UN,' used by first responders and listed in the US DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, a tank endorsement is required for a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons (and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more)?
choice_a: 100 gallons
choice_b: 119 gallons
choice_c: 150 gallons
choice_d: 1,000 gallons
explanation: The manual requires a tank endorsement for any vehicle designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, 2.23.3 Lists of Regulated Products
